evals.prompt: You are running the Codex autopilot and you are about to fan out work to subagents — for example a Phase 7 batch of [P]-marked tasks, or consensus analysts across several queued items. Describe how you detect the current collaboration surface, respect its concurrency limit, and complete each dispatch. Cover both a local Codex surface that exposes close_agent and hosted Responses Multi-agent, which does not. Also state what you check before reporting completion and how you handle a stuck subagent.
evals.expected_output: Capability-detects collaboration actions. On hosted Responses, send_message queues context and followup_task assigns work and starts a turn. On a local surface, send_input delivers follow-up work to an open agent; a closed agent requires resume_agent followed by send_input. Requires spawn_agent -> a bounded wait_agent loop -> consume the dispatched agent's actual final result on every surface; ordinary messages, timeouts, and terminal status do not replace the summary. If close_agent is exposed, calls it best-effort after consuming the result and does not retry-loop already-gone. If absent, does not stop: hosted Responses Multi-agent exposes no close action, so the host retains the inspectable completed thread. Derives subagent_slots from the current surface, subtracting root from total-agent counts and using one when no count is exposed, then dispatches wider fan-out in waves. One wait timeout is only a poll boundary. interrupt_agent is only for a confirmed stuck running turn, preserves context, and requires the item to be re-spawned and return a real result. Audits list_agents when exposed or tracked task/result evidence otherwise before completion.
expectations: Capability-detects the collaboration actions before dispatch and does not hard-stop merely because close_agent is absent
Maps hosted followup_task to assigning work and local send_input to follow-up delivery; a closed local agent uses resume_agent then send_input
Names spawn_agent -> bounded wait_agent loop -> consume the actual final result as the required cross-surface lifecycle
States that ordinary mailbox messages, timeouts, and terminal status cannot replace the required agent summary
Derives subagent_slots from the current surface, subtracts one when a total-agent count includes root, and falls back safely to one when no count is exposed
Dispatches fan-out wider than the cap in waves instead of spawning all work in one turn
When close_agent is exposed, treats cleanup as best-effort and does not retry-loop an already-gone result
When close_agent is absent, leaves the completed inspectable thread to the host without stopping
Treats one wait_agent timeout as a poll boundary rather than proof the agent is stuck
Uses interrupt_agent only for a confirmed stuck running turn and states interruption is neither closure nor a result
Requires any interrupted required item to be re-spawned and return a real result before completion
Before reporting completion, audits list_agents when exposed or tracked dispatch IDs and consumed results otherwise

evals.prompt: During the Codex autopilot, the implement-executor needs to match a new payment-retry module to the repo's existing error-handling pattern. Several capabilities could help. How does it decide which one to use to gather that codebase context, and what governs the choice?

Capability categories are a taxonomy, not an ordered fallback chain. A formerly named tool is used only when discovery selects it as the best available capability for that need.
expectations: States the needed capability category is identified first (codebase context) before any tool is chosen
Selects the best INSTALLED capability for that need by task fit and evidence quality

evals.prompt: In a Codex autopilot run, two findings were resolved: finding A used a high-fit installed capability with a direct authoritative source; finding B fell back to local files because no installed capability covered the need. How must the Confidence on each finding compare, and why?
evals.expected_output: Confidence is calibrated to evidence quality, so it is lower for the fallback finding. Finding A may carry high confidence because a high-fit installed capability supplied a direct, authoritative source. Finding B, resolved by fallback because no installed capability covered the need, MUST be reported at medium or low confidence — fallback evidence is never reported as high confidence — and carries the fallback disclosure line stating the missing capability, the local/native/repo-local fallback used, and the reason. Lower fallback quality yields a lower, explicitly calibrated confidence.
expectations: States the fallback finding (B) is reported at medium or low confidence, never high
States the high-fit finding (A) may carry high confidence because a direct authoritative source backed it
Ties the confidence difference to evidence quality / source directness rather than to which named tool was used
Requires finding B to carry the fallback disclosure naming the missing capability, the fallback used, and the reason
